title: Windows, PowerShell & VS Code Operations Core v1

domain.name: Windows, PowerShell & VS Code Operations
domain.description: Practical Windows administration, PowerShell automation, VS Code workspace operation, paths, processes, environments, permissions, diagnostics, and safe system changes.

competencies.name: Windows Files, Paths & Storage
competencies.description: Understand drive letters, absolute and relative paths, permissions, links, and storage layout.
competencies.purpose: Navigate and automate Windows storage safely.

units.title: Paths have context
units.content: Relative paths depend on the current working directory; environment variables, mapped drives, external disks, and links can make the same-looking command behave differently.

units.title: File operation workflow
units.content: Resolve the intended absolute path; inspect existence and type; verify destination; prefer copy before destructive move when uncertain; validate result; only then remove superseded data if permitted.

units.title: Path failures
units.content: Avoid assuming current directory, writing to system folders accidentally, confusing shortcuts with files, and destructive wildcard commands without a preview.

drills.title: Debug a broken external-drive path
drills.prompt: Given a script that works on C: but fails on E:, identify path, permissions, and environment checks.

competencies.name: PowerShell Objects, Pipeline & StrictMode
competencies.description: Use object-based pipelines, properties, filtering, formatting, and StrictMode safely.
competencies.purpose: Write scripts that behave predictably instead of depending on display text.

units.title: PowerShell pipelines pass objects
units.content: Cmdlets usually emit structured objects; formatting commands are for display and should not be used as data transformations.

units.title: Pipeline workflow
units.content: Inspect objects and properties; filter and transform structured data; avoid parsing formatted tables; enable strict error handling in automation.

units.title: Pipeline failures
units.content: Avoid piping Format-Table into later logic, silently accessing missing properties, relying on aliases in production scripts, and swallowing errors that should stop the workflow.

drills.title: Rewrite a brittle PowerShell pipeline
drills.prompt: Replace text parsing and aliases with object-safe logic and strict error handling.

competencies.name: Processes, Services & System Diagnostics
competencies.description: Inspect running processes, services, ports, environment variables, and resource usage.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose local development and application failures methodically.

units.title: Diagnostic workflow
units.content: Observe symptoms; identify process or service ownership; inspect PID, command line, port bindings, logs, and resource use; change one variable at a time; document restart or configuration changes.

units.title: Inspect before killing
units.content: A process holding a port may be the service you need; identify it before termination.

units.title: Diagnostic failures
units.content: Avoid killing unknown system processes, restarting many services at once, changing firewall settings before confirming the cause, and treating high CPU as proof of malware.

drills.title: Diagnose a port conflict
drills.prompt: Work through a local API that cannot bind to its expected port.

competencies.name: Environment Variables & Runtime Dependencies
competencies.description: Manage PATH, per-project environments, runtime versions, and dependency discovery.
competencies.purpose: Keep development tools reproducible across shells and projects.

units.title: Environment state is scoped
units.content: User, system, process, shell, virtual environment, and project-level settings can disagree; a tool visible in one terminal may be absent in another.

units.title: Environment diagnosis
units.content: Check executable resolution; inspect PATH and relevant variables; identify active Python, Node, or Conda environment; compare project expectations; make the smallest scoped change.

units.title: Environment failures
units.content: Avoid permanently editing system PATH for a temporary need, mixing multiple Python environments unintentionally, and assuming an installed package belongs to the active interpreter.

drills.title: Diagnose a runtime mismatch
drills.prompt: Trace why one PowerShell window finds Python dependencies and another does not.

competencies.name: VS Code Workspaces, Tasks & Debugging
competencies.description: Use workspaces, settings, tasks, terminals, launch configurations, and extensions consistently.
competencies.purpose: Turn the editor into a repeatable project cockpit.

units.title: Workspace setup
units.content: Open the correct folder or workspace; define project-local settings where justified; configure tasks for common commands; configure launch/debug entry points; keep secrets out of settings; document required extensions.

units.title: Project settings beat machine folklore
units.content: Critical build and debug behavior should live in the repo when safe, not only in remembered local editor clicks.

units.title: VS Code failures
units.content: Avoid globally changing settings to fix one repo, storing tokens in settings files, and relying on a terminal whose working directory is wrong.

drills.title: Design a FREEOS VS Code workspace
drills.prompt: Plan tasks for build, dev, tests, and logs plus safe local settings.

competencies.name: Permissions, UAC & Safe Elevation
competencies.description: Recognize when Windows permissions or elevation are required and minimize privileged changes.
competencies.purpose: Avoid unsafe administrator usage while completing legitimate system tasks.

units.title: Administrator is a capability boundary
units.content: Elevation can modify protected files, services, firewall rules, drivers, and system configuration; use it only for the exact operation that requires it.

units.title: Safe elevation workflow
units.content: Confirm the operation and target; determine whether elevation is truly required; record current state; elevate only the scoped command or tool; verify the result; return to standard context.

units.title: Elevation failures
units.content: Avoid running entire development environments as administrator, disabling security controls to bypass a permission problem, and applying recursive ownership changes without understanding scope.

drills.title: Decide whether to elevate
drills.prompt: For several Windows setup tasks, identify which require elevation and how to scope it.

competencies.name: Logs, Event Viewer & Failure Evidence
competencies.description: Use application logs, Windows logs, command output, and timestamps to identify causes.
competencies.purpose: Diagnose from evidence rather than repeated guessing.

units.title: Evidence workflow
units.content: Capture exact error text and time; inspect application logs first; correlate with Windows or system events when relevant; search by component or error signature; preserve first-failure evidence before retries change state.

units.title: The first error is often more valuable than the last
units.content: Cascading failures can bury the initiating problem; find the earliest relevant failure in the chain.

units.title: Logging failures
units.content: Avoid clearing logs before diagnosis, sharing secrets from logs, focusing on unrelated warnings, and changing configuration before recording the original error.

drills.title: Investigate a startup failure
drills.prompt: Build an evidence checklist for an app that exits immediately on Windows.

competencies.name: Safe Windows Automation & Rollback
competencies.description: Automate repetitive local work with idempotence, previews, validation, and rollback.
competencies.purpose: Scale scripts without turning small mistakes into system-wide damage.

units.title: Automation safety pattern
units.content: Validate inputs; resolve exact targets; provide dry-run or preview for destructive or wide operations; make changes idempotently; log actions; verify postconditions; preserve rollback information.

units.title: Wide scope requires stronger proof
units.content: A script touching hundreds of files, registry entries, or services should require more validation than one changing a single known file.

units.title: Automation failures
units.content: Avoid recursive delete or move from unvalidated variables, irreversible registry edits, silent overwrite, and scripts that continue after failed prerequisites.

drills.title: Review a risky maintenance script
drills.prompt: Define safeguards for a script that moves caches, edits PATH, and restarts services.
